newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: New Ireland 1996 pre-tax profit falls.
newsitem.headline: New Ireland 1996 pre-tax profit falls.

text.p: Irish-based insurance company New Ireland Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that 1996 pre-tax profit fell to 5.16 million Irish pounds from 10.39 million a year earlier after a 5.8 million punt reversal on its general insurance company results.

But the group said it had very strong growth in its life assurance and financial services subsidiaries in 1996 and the embedded value of New Ireland Assurance, its life company, increased by 15 percent to 117.8 million Irish pounds.

New Ireland, which announced the sale of its general insurance company Irish National to Eagle Star in February, said it will now concentrate its activities on the life and pensions market in Ireland which it believes offers good prospects for long-term growth.
Last year, total new annual premium business rose by 18 percent to 21.8 million Irish pounds with new pensions business increasing by 26 percent to 11.1 million.
Single premium business rose by 27 percent to 118.6 million.
New Ireland said investment returns in the financial markets in Ireland were "extremely good" last year with Irish bonds and equities showing returns of 13 percent and 26 percent respectively.
Profit before tax in the life company totalled 7.2 million against 7.1 million in 1995.

But the general insurance market in Ireland remained extremely competitive in 1996 with the personal lines market characterised by continued underpricing of motor business together with increased claims costs and increases in road accidents and road deaths, New Ireland said.

As a consequence, the company experienced an increased underwriting loss on its private motor account in 1996 although the performance of the corporate lines account, in particular the fire account, was satisfactory.

Total premium income slipped to 74.8 million Irish pounds from 77.8 million in 1995 and the underwriting deficit increased to 10 million from 5.8 million a year earlier, resulting in a pre-tax loss of 2.6 million.

Aided by the buoyancy of financial markets, New Ireland Financial Services Ltd, the group's specialist financial services subsidiary, reported an increase in pre-tax profit to 1.47 million Irish pounds from 0.93 million a year earlier.
New Ireland announced a 10 percent increase in its dividend to a net total of 18.56 pence per share.
The company is part of a group created last year by Sun Life and Provincial Holdings and which also includes Sun Life and UAP Provincial.
